calculator.title: Spoke-body axial elongation calculator
calculator.areaPresetNote: This area is locked to the backend catalogue preset. Choose Custom effective area to edit it.
calculator.lengthNote: Enter only the spoke body's loaded axial length here; no whole-wheel geometry is required. An initial 290 mm value is prefilled for convenience; replace it with the measured loaded length.
calculator.overloadStressNote: Used for comparison with the material macro-yield reference
calculator.workElongationLabel: Recoverable elastic elongation at working tension
calculator.overloadElongationLabel: Recoverable elastic elongation at overload reference
calculator.elasticElongationNote: L={length} mm, A={area} mm², E={modulus} MPa; about {micrometres} μm. The elastic part theoretically returns on unloading; plastic elongation is excluded.
calculator.pendingResult: Waiting for the authoritative backend result
calculator.scopeTitle: Model scope: axial elongation of the spoke itself
calculator.scopeDescription: This calculator covers only the spoke metal body's axial elastic elongation at the specified tension. It uses effective loaded length L, effective area A, and material modulus E with ΔL = F × L / (A × E) to report recoverable elongation. It does not turn work hardening, plastic strain, necking, or fracture into a fixed threshold; those stages require the complete stress–strain curve for the defined wire condition. It also omits spoke-to-rim angle, local rim layup, spoke-hole or hole-seat denting, local hole-edge deformation, washer or copper-insert compression, and contact seating. Total wheel tension loss is outside this calculation and requires measurement.
calculator.rimReferenceTitle: How to use the {rimBaseline} N reference baseline
calculator.rimReferenceDescription: {rimBaseline} N is a self-set carbon-rim spoke-hole baseline for calculation and comparison on this page, not a factory test standard, rim certification value, or universal safety limit. Factory tests commonly use near-vertical loading, while spokes in a built wheel meet the rim at an angle; test results are therefore useful context but cannot be treated as conclusive or converted directly into built-wheel hole-seat capacity. This page omits whole-wheel angle effects and keeps the spoke's axial elongation/stress relationship reusable for spoke-length calculations.

safety.invalidDescription: The backend rejected the current input. Check that tension, effective area, and overload ratio stay within the backend's published bounds; no local estimate is substituted.
safety.unavailableDescription: The authoritative backend result is temporarily unavailable. No local estimate is substituted; please try again later.
safety.loadingDescription: The browser is waiting for the authoritative Go calculation result.
safety.criticalTitle: Critical: above the page's self-set reference baseline
safety.criticalDescription: The model reaches {overload} N with {stress} MPa instantaneous stress ({ratio}% of the yield reference). Its signed margin to the page's self-set {rimBaseline} N spoke-hole baseline is {rimMargin} N; this is not a rim-failure determination and must not be used alone for workshop loading.
safety.warningTitle: Warning: approaching the page's self-set high-load baseline
safety.warningDescription: The model reaches {overload} N and {stress} MPa. It is approaching the page's self-set spoke-hole comparison baseline; the actual rim, spoke angle, factory test method, and manufacturer limits must control the build.
safety.safeDescription: The model reaches {overload} N and leaves {margin}% to the page's self-set {rimBaseline} N spoke-hole baseline. This is a spoke-body elongation/stress calculation state, not a rim certification conclusion or universal tension recommendation.

calculator.boundary: The backend material profile uses {uts} MPa as an engineering tensile-strength reference and {yieldReference} MPa as an engineering macro-yield reference for cold-drawn AISI 302/304. They describe the defined material family and condition; they are not measured certificates for a particular brand or model.
calculator.torsion: Residual nipple wind-up adds to the equivalent von Mises stress. Use a spoke-holding tool and the exact assembly procedure for the selected flat or double-butted spoke.
calculator.materialReferenceTitle: Generic materials-science profile (shared by current models):
calculator.materialReferenceDescription: All current models intentionally use the cold-drawn/cold-worked stainless-steel profile "{name}". Material catalogue version {catalogVersion}, profile data version {dataVersion}, status {status}. It describes the defined material family and manufacturing condition, not a product certificate for a particular brand or model; update the catalogue when traceable supplier or test data for a defined product condition becomes available.
calculator.materialReferenceBasis: The profile defines {family} in the condition "{condition}". These values have different roles: {modulus} MPa is the elastic-modulus reference for cold-drawn austenitic 302/304 wire and is used directly by the spoke-body elongation formula; {yieldReference} MPa is the engineering macro-yield reference for this condition and is used for the page's stress ratio; {ultimateStrength} MPa is the engineering tensile-strength reference shown in the material profile. They are not measured certificates for a particular SAPIM, Pillar, or DT Swiss model, and they are not identical for every 302/304 wire. This calculator uses the material parameters above and does not add a separate dislocation value.

materialReferenceStatuses.genericMaterialsScience: Generic materials-science reference (cold-drawn austenitic stainless steel)

calculator.intro: Every input is sent to the Go backend, and the page displays only the returned stress, force, and recoverable elastic elongation of one spoke body. A selected model locks its effective area to the versioned catalogue; choose Custom effective area only when you have a measured value. “Cold-drawn/cold-worked” describes the wire manufacturing condition; it does not mean that this calculator simulates work hardening during the current load.
calculator.formulaNote: F is the axial spoke force, L the loaded spoke-body length, A the effective load-bearing area, and E the backend material modulus.

materialLadder.title: Single-spoke materials load ladder and reference window
materialLadder.description: The ladder follows the current backend result. It locates the spoke body against material references without treating rim test loads as certification limits.
materialLadder.workingDescription: Current working stress {stress}; the starting point for the spoke-body elastic calculation.
materialLadder.overloadDescription: Calculated with the current {ratio}% ratio to show the stress-relief reference state.
materialLadder.rimDescription: A comparison reference on this page, not a factory test standard, certification value, or universal safety limit.
materialLadder.yieldDescription: From the backend cold-drawn austenitic stainless-steel profile; this is stress, not a product certificate.
materialLadder.note: These steps describe the single spoke body tension–stress–elongation relationship. The actual build still requires the rim, hole seat, spoke angle, and manufacturer limits.

microstructure.title: Microstructural dislocation evolution in cold-drawn stainless steel
microstructure.description: Cold-drawn austenitic stainless steel (SUS302/304) has a high dislocation density. The diagram explains dislocation motion and pile-up around the stress-relief reference state.
